scene_jp: <ruby>老人<rt>ろうじん</rt></ruby>はしばらく<ruby>黙<rt>だま</rt></ruby>っていた。「……どのおばあさんのことだ？」と、<ruby>低<rt>ひく</rt></ruby>い<ruby>声<rt>こえ</rt></ruby>で<ruby>聞<rt>き</rt></ruby>いてくる。<ruby>店<rt>みせ</rt></ruby>の<ruby>奥<rt>おく</rt></ruby>で、<ruby>古<rt>ふる</rt></ruby>い<ruby>時計<rt>とけい</rt></ruby>がカチカチと<ruby>音<rt>おと</rt></ruby>を<ruby>立<rt>た</rt></ruby>てている。<ruby>老人<rt>ろうじん</rt></ruby>の<ruby>目<rt>め</rt></ruby>には、<ruby>恐<rt>おそ</rt></ruby>れというより、<ruby>諦<rt>あきら</rt></ruby>めのような<ruby>色<rt>いろ</rt></ruby>が<ruby>浮<rt>う</rt></ruby>かんでいた。「その<ruby>人<rt>ひと</rt></ruby>が<ruby>何<rt>なに</rt></ruby>かを<ruby>話<rt>はな</rt></ruby>したなら、もうここに<ruby>来<rt>き</rt></ruby>てしまったんだ——<ruby>逃<rt>に</rt></ruby>げるわけにもいかん」と<ruby>老人<rt>ろうじん</rt></ruby>はつぶやいた。
scene_translation: The old man was silent for a moment. "…Which old woman do you mean?" he asked in a low voice. In the back of the shop, an old clock ticked steadily. In the old man's eyes, there was less fear than something that looked like resignation. "If that person told you something, then you've already come here — there's no running away from it," the old man murmured.
grammar_note: 【わけにもいかん】A contracted form of わけにもいかない — 'there's no way I can / it's out of the question to do.' The pattern Verb-dictionary + わけにはいかない expresses that doing something is socially, morally, or practically impossible. Here the old man uses the blunter いかん (older/masculine speech) instead of いかない, which also reflects his rough register. Compare: 嘘をつくわけにはいかない (I can't very well lie).

vocab.meaning: to be silent, to say nothing
to float up, to appear (on one's face)
colour; here: expression, look (in one's eyes)

feedback: Good effort — you clearly communicated the meaning! The natural phrasing would be おばあさんから聞きました (きいた → きいた is fine as a plain past form, but です doesn't attach directly to a verb in standard Japanese). You could also say おばあさんに教えてもらいました ('an old woman told me') for a slightly more natural feel. Don't worry — the old man understood you perfectly.

mystery_memo: The old shopkeeper (じいさん) has now confirmed he was expecting someone to come — a mysterious old woman sent the player here, and he seems to have resigned himself to this meeting. He knows something about the woman from Scene 1 and about the player's presence. The recurring mystery figure is likely the same woman seen at Tokyo Station. The player's answer (heard from an old woman) has shifted the shopkeeper from fearful/evasive to reluctantly cooperative — relationship moves from suspicious toward neutral-wary. No new items this scene, but the ticking clock in the back of the shop is a potential detail to revisit.
